text: The assembly will hear an address by his
excellency Denise Biroich, chairman of
the presidency of Bosnaguia.
I request protocol to escort his
excellency and invite him to address the
assembly.
Dear President of the United Nations
General Assembly,
respected Secretary General of the
United Nations,
Excellencies,
ladies and gentlemen,
it is an honor and a pleasure to address
the 81st session of the UN General
Assembly on behalf of Bosnia and
Herziggoina.
We are a symbol of a nation that has
survived severe trials but has not lost
its path towards a better future.
In the period from 1992 to 1995,
my country was subjected to aggression,
joint criminal enterprises, genocide
against Bosnjaks, crimes against
humanity, and other war crimes.
Following the end of the aggression in
destructive forces have sought through
blockades, obstruction, and other means
to halt the progress of Bosnia and
Hergoina.
They are slowing down our path towards a
modern European state, but they cannot
stop it.
Today, Bosnia Intersegoina stands at the
doorstep of the European Union and the
NATO. These are our strategic foreign
policy objectives unanimously defined by
the state authorities of Bosnia and
Heriggoina.
Unfortunately, there are still those
seeking to realize
greater state projects at the expense of
the territory of Bosnia and Hergoina.
During the aggression they attacked our
country by military means today
they do so by political, diplomatic and
other means. It is very important that
the UN courts have established the
nature of the war waged against the
Republic of Bosnia and Hergoina.
Final judgments, including those
concerning joint criminal enterprises,
have established that this was an
international armed conflict.
Judgments of the highest UN courts have
established that genocide was committed
against Bosnjaks.
They also stand as judgments on the
greater state policies that through a
joint criminal enterprise
sought to divide and destroy Bosnian
as an independent, sovereign,
indivisible and internationally
recognized state.
Ladies and gentlemen,
we live in a world of injustice,
insecurity, and intolerance.
the strengthening of authoritarian
populism, the aggression against
Ukraine, the suffering in Gaza, the war
in the Gulf region, the catastrophic
situation in Sudan, and other flash
points have brought humanity into a
profound crisis marked by great
uncertainty and fear.
We must not remain silent in the face of
injustice.
The world did not respond adequately to
the aggression against Ukraine and the
genocide against Palestinians in Gaza,
just as it did not during the aggression
against Bosnia and Hergoina.
The aggression of the Russian Federation
against Ukraine is a flagrant example of
a violation of the UN charter and
international law. While Gaza is
humanity's greatest defeat in the 21st
century,
the greatest global crisis are directly
interconnected and have the same route.
The erosion of international law.
Disrespect for international law cannot
lead the world towards prosperity and a
better future. Ladies and gentlemen,
without identifying the causes of the
crisis facing contemporary humanity, we
cannot solve its problems. The politics
of force cannot bring progress to
humanity.
Instead of force, we need respect and
the strengthening of the existing
international norms, rules and
institutions that we have built over
more than 80 years. The multilateral
system today faces a serious challenge,
a crisis of institutional trust. Trust
is weakening because some actors in the
international community undermine the
values enshrined in the UN charter. The
future of humanity does not lie in
policies of violence and human rights
violations.
Conflicts and wars are not the purpose
of our civilization. Let us build a
culture of dialogue, cooperation and
peace. In this context, I believe it is
of utmost importance to reaffirm the
importance of the UN charter, revitalize
the role of the UN as the global center
for coordination and cooperation.
Support the reform process and
strengthen the credibility of the United
Nations. Consistently implement the
sustainable development goals. build
mutual trust, inclusiveness and
democratic vision of leadership and
strengthen preventive diplomacy at a
time of numerous tensions and conflicts.
Let respect for international law,
peace, solidarity, sustainable
development and justice be the path that
we follow together.
Ladies and gentlemen,
we in Bosnia and Herzgoina call upon all
UN member states to focus on reaffirming
relations between states on the basis of
international law, ensuring respect for
human rights and fundamental freedoms,
promoting peace and social progress,
combating hate speech and all forms of
discrimination, strengthening policies
for the prevention of genocide, crimes
against humanity and other war crimes,
advancing the rights of women and
children, and strengthening gender
equality, better health care and
education.
The world must return to the fundamental
principles upon which the UN is founded.
Respect for human dignity, the sovereign
equality of states, the peaceful
settlement of disputes, respect for
international law. These are not
unrealistic propositions.
They are the only possible foundations
of a stable world. Bosnia and Segoina is
a reliable and responsible member of the
United Nations. Among other things, I
would like to remind that Bosnia
desergoina is aware of climate change
and committed to contributing to global
efforts, committed to the transition
towards renewable energy sources and the
reduction of harmful gas emissions and
determined to combat all forms of
terrorism.
We in Bosnia desergoina know that peace
cannot be taken for granted. Peace.
Peace must be safeguarded every day. It
requires responsibility of political
leaders, respect for the law and
readiness for dialogue.
There must not be one standard for large
states and another for small states. If
we want to preserve trust in the
international order, the rules we
establish together must be applied
equally.
Ladies and gentlemen,
Bosnia and Herzgoina is the only country
in Europe where genocide was committed
after the Second World War. In May 2024,
the UN General Assembly adopted the
resolution designating
11th July as the International Day of
Reflection and Commemoration of the 1995
genocide in Sreita.
This resolution represents a profoundly
moral and civilizational act by the UN
General Assembly. The adopted resolution
is equally important for the UN and for
Bosnia and Hergoina.
It is particularly dangerous that the
leadership of the Republic of Serbia
glorifies the convicted war criminal Rat
Kumladic.
The monster Rat Kumladic is not a hero
but a convicted war criminal. The
institutional glorification of this war
criminal is an anti-ivilizational and
unacceptable act. It amounts to
identifying Serbia's state leadership
with one of the worst butchers in
European history. It is an indication
that Serbia has not abandoned the
ideology and policies that lead to
aggression and genocide. It is a direct
assault on the values of the United
Nations whose court delivered a final
judgment against this war criminal.
Let me remind you that Serbia is the
only state in the world that has been
found by a UN court to have violated the
UN convention on the prevention and
punishment of the crime of genocide.
I call on the United Nations and
European Union and other international
actors to clearly condemn this conduct
and take concrete measures against those
who institutionally glorify convicted
war criminals.
Unfortunately, the ideology and policies
that led to genocide against Bosnjaks
continue to threaten Bosnia and
Desgoina.
From the podium of the UN General
Assembly, I wish to publicly warn the
international public that the current
leadership of the Bosnian entity,
Republica,
continues to threaten the peace and
security of Bosnian Duggoina and the
region. We must stop this destructive
policy together. The victims of the
genocide and the employees of the
memorial centers Reberita
are facing unacceptable pressures from
the police of the Republic Serpska.
We must not allow that the police and
other institutions of Republica Serpska
which committed the genocide against
Bosnjaks
today threaten the survivors and those
that are preserving the memory on the
victims of the genocide. Those
seeking to destroy the Dayton peace
agreement are attempting to create the
conditions for the secession of the
Bosnian entity Republicska.
In the period ahead, they will intensify
their activities primarily with the aim
of weakening and abolishing the mandate
of the high representative of the
international community which is also
envisaged by the daton peace agreement,
weakening the institution of the
constitutional court of Bosnian dergoina
and seizing the state property of
Bosnian deruggoina contrary to the
national and international law. Ladies
and gentlemen,
Bosnia and Herzgoina is an unconquerable
state. There is not a single map of
southeast Europe from the past 1,000
years on which Bosnia or Bosnia and
Suggoina does not appear.
Bosnia and Dergoina is home to people
who love freedom more than their own
lives. Finally, as the chairman of the
presidency of Bosian desergoina, I wish
to emphasize that I'm proud of the brave
people of Bosian Suggoina. These are
people who have suffered injustice, yet
they continue to fight for justice.
These are people who have been victims
of lies, yet they continue to fight for
the truth. These are people who support
the struggle for justice, freedom, and
human dignity throughout the world.
These are the honorable and proud people
of my homeland, Bosnia and Herzgoina.
Thank you for your attention.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish thank
the chairman of the presidency of Bosnia
and Heriggoia
